data.gender_notes: Haramiyah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'haram', meaning sacred, and the suffix 'iyah' which signifies protector. Haramiyah is a name for a girl who is a guardian of the sacred. The name Haramiyah carries the meaning “Protector of the sacred” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Haramiyah usually hope their child will grow to embody protector of the sacred and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Haramiyah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Protector of the sacred.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Haramiyah total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: حَرمِيَة
in_arabic.meaning: المكان المُحَرّم، الأَمور المُحَرَمة، المَكان المَخصّص
in_arabic.long_meaning: حَرَمِيَةً أَو حَرَمٌ مُحَرَّمٌ أَو مَكانٌ مُحَرَّمٌ، وَهِيَ مِنَ الاسماءِ الَّتي تُعربُ بِالفتحِ، وَتُكَفِّلُ حَرَماً بِالمُحَرَّمِ، وَبِالأَمورِ المُحَرَمةِ، وَهِيَ مِنَ الاسماءِ اللاتي يُؤتِى فضلُها في الدُنيَا وَالآخِرَةِ، وَهِيَ أَمّا الدنيا فَهِيَ مِنَ الأَماني، وَفيها بِالرِزقِ الَّذي يُريدهُ، وَفيها بِالنَجاحِ في الأُمورِ، وَفيها بِالتَوفيقِ، وَهِيَ أَمّا الآخِرَةَ فَهِيَ مِنَ الأَنامِلِ، وَهِيَ مِنَ الأَماني المُستَقبَلَةِ، وَهِيَ مِنَ الأَماني المُتَوَقَّعةِ، وَهِيَ مِنَ الأَماني المُتَحَمِّلَةِ

in_urdu.name: ہرمیہ
in_urdu.meaning: محرم مقام، محرم امور، مخصوص مقام
in_urdu.long_meaning: ہرمیہ یا حرام، محرم مقام، محرم امور، مخصوص مقام ہے۔ یہ اسماءً فعلہ ہے جو فعل حرم کی اول صورت سے ماخوذ ہے، یہ اسم فاعل ہے اور اس کے معنی محرم مقام یا امور ہیں۔ اس کے معنی میں سے ایک یہ بھی شامل ہے کہ یہ مخصوص مقام ہے، کہ یہ محرم مقام ہے اور اس میں داخل ہونے یا اس سے کچھ کرنا حرام ہے۔

in_hindi.name: हारमिया

in_english.name: Haramiyah
in_english.meaning: Forbidden place, forbidden things, special place
in_english.long_meaning: Haramiyah or Haram, forbidden place, forbidden things, special place. Derived from the Arabic root ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m), meaning 'to forbid' or 'to prohibit', this name conveys a sense of sanctity and restriction. In Islamic tradition, haram refers to actions, objects, or places that are forbidden or prohibited. It is a term used to describe the sacred and the prohibited. In the context of Islamic law, haram is used to describe things that are forbidden or unlawful, such as murder, theft, and adultery. In a broader sense, haram can refer to anything that is considered impure or unholy.
